approach: Add Priority::Urgent (sorts before High) with from_text/as_str/parse. Add per-job record kind athena.priority/1 (priority-<n>.json) loaded into JobRecords.priorities; one JobRecords::priority() resolves latest priority record, else request `Priority:` line, else Urgent if latest reading has urgent_reason, else Normal; plan_entry and status::job_line both call it. Athena::set_priority (store.rs) requires Queued, validates level, commits one record; CLI `athena priority <job> <level>`. ReadingOutput and Reading gain urgent_reason: Option<String> (Reading side serde default, skipped when None); the urgent-marking rule is a doc comment on the ReadingOutput field in outputs.rs (schema description), reader.md untouched. Fake reader marks speed-up requests. Append D122 after D121 only, CHANGELOG entry, and a decisions-log guard test in decisions.rs that checks structure and a pinned hash of the base-length prefix.

decisions.choice: New record kind athena.priority/1, latest by n wins
decisions.reason: Request records must not be rewritten; records are append-only; D118 named this design.

decisions.choice: Single JobRecords::priority() used by plan and status
Urgent rule as doc comment on ReadingOutput.urgent_reason in outputs.rs
decisions.reason: Becomes schema description; reader.md is at 1997/2000 tokens and must not grow.

rejected.why: Keeping rule with field is clearer.

decisions.choice: Pin base decisions.md by byte length 230046 and SHA-256 of that prefix
decisions.reason: Tests cannot see the base commit; prefix hash proves existing entries are byte-identical while allowing end additions.

rejected.why: Base ref unknown at test time.

steps: Compute SHA-256 and length of base docs/decisions.md via git show HEAD:docs/decisions.md before editing.

risks.risk: Repeating the D121/D122 damage by mid-file edit.
risks.mitigation: Single append at end; guard test and git diff show no earlier byte changed.
Rule in schema doc comment; reader.md unchanged; run budgets test.

risks.risk: New Reading field breaks struct literals and old records.
risks.mitigation: serde default and skip when None; update every Reading literal.

risks.risk: Reading-derived Urgent overriding an explicit text priority.
risks.mitigation: Precedence in one method: record, text, reading, normal.

risks.risk: Pinned hash computed from the edited file.
risks.mitigation: Compute from git show HEAD:docs/decisions.md before editing; note derivation in test comment.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests in plan.rs build entries with Urgent, High, Normal and an urgent entry depending on a normal one; assert Plan::build order.
demonstrations.observes: Order is urgent, high, normal; the dependency precedes its urgent dependent.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without Urgent sorting before High or the dependency rule, the ordering assertions fail.

demonstrations.method: Test: queued job with request `Priority: low` gets an urgent priority record via set_priority; load records, build plan and status line.
demonstrations.observes: Plan puts job first, status shows urgent, request.json unchanged, exactly one new priority-1.json.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the record were ignored, order and status stay at low; if a request were rewritten the file-count/bytes assertion fails.

demonstrations.method: Reading tests parse ReadingOutput with an urgent reason and with null, run build_reading; fake-agent test with a speed-improving and an ordinary request.
demonstrations.observes: Some(reason) recorded for urgent and speed request, None for null and ordinary; plan priority urgent only for the first.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the field deny_unknown_fields rejects the output; without build_reading wiring the Reading lacks the reason; without the fake rule the speed request is unmarked.

demonstrations.method: Tests call set_priority with `bogus`, unknown job, non-queued job; assert errors and no commit; assert Priority::from_text("Priority: urgent")==Urgent; render help and check for 'urgent' and 'priority'.
demonstrations.observes: Clear errors, no record committed, urgent parsed, help mentions both words.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without validation bad input commits a record; without the parse arm urgent stays Normal.

demonstrations.method: Test in outputs.rs generates the reading schema and checks the urgent_reason description contains the rule terms; git diff on reader.md shows nothing.
demonstrations.observes: Description contains faster, failed or rejected attempts, planning stops, timeouts, redo, thrash, duplicated checks, reason required.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the rule were absent from the schema the description assertion fails.

demonstrations.method: Run the existing budgets test unchanged.
demonstrations.observes: Reader set at or under 2000 tokens.
demonstrations.fails_without: A rule added to reader.md would push the reader set over 2000 tokens and fail.

demonstrations.method: Test in decisions.rs parses docs/decisions.md into `## D<n> · ` entries, checks Provenance, unique ascending ids, and SHA-256 of the first 230046 bytes against the pinned base hash; negative cases on small strings.
demonstrations.observes: All checks pass on the final file; negative cases return errors.
demonstrations.fails_without: A mid-file insertion, duplicate or descending id, missing Provenance, or edit of the first 230046 bytes fails the guard.

demonstrations.method: Inspect the diff of the two docs.
demonstrations.observes: decisions.md diff is additions only after D121 (new D122 with alternatives and Provenance); CHANGELOG has a new entry; no removed lines.

demonstrations.method: Run the three gate commands; each must exit 0. The full test run includes every new test above, so it exercises all behaviors.
demonstrations.observes: cargo fmt --all --check, cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings and cargo test --locked all exit 0.
demonstrations.fails_without: If any new behavior were missing or broken, its new test in the full cargo test run fails; unformatted code fails fmt --check; warnings (e.g. an unused or unhandled new Priority variant or unupdated Reading literal) fail clippy or compilation.

open_questions: Whether a prefix hash is acceptable as the 'against the base commit' check, since cargo test cannot see the base commit.
Exact trigger words for the fake reader's speed-improving requests.
Whether display.rs shows urgent without edits (expected, it prints any non-normal priority).
